mainTopic: Measuring a skull's missing piece (drill-hole versus סלע), the testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש on the inside and outside of vessels, and the start of the משנה on eye blemishes.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a challenge: a drill-hole equals a סלע, so בית שמאי and בית הלל would give the same size for a skull with a missing piece. רב חסדא answers that the measure is 'a drill and its חיסום,' a hole with room for the drill to go in and out. רב תחליפא calls this as certain as the testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש. The גמרא quotes that testimony and challenges it, because a כלי חרס with no inside cannot become טמא at all. רבי יצחק בר אבין explains that it is really about a כלי שטף. With no inside, its sides are one. With an inside, it works like a כלי חרס. The גמרא explains that this inside/outside split applies only to rabbinic טומאת משקין, and that חז"ל shaped it as a היכירא so people would not burn תרומה and קדשים. The גמרא then returns to the skull: רב פפא says the drill equal to a סלע was a large drill, and רב נחמן says the matching סלע was a large Neronian one, so בית שמאי stay the stricter side. Finally, a new משנה begins listing eye blemishes, including damage to the eyelid and the תבלול.

steps.title: The challenge ends and the questioned רב תחליפא is silent
steps.stepSummary: The challenge ends by showing that a drill-hole is 'like the hole of a yoke.' This makes the measure of בית שמאי equal to the סלע of בית הלל. רב תחליפא has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Like the full size of the hole of a yoke!' He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge: a drill-hole is the size of a yoke-hole, which comes out the same as a סלע. רב תחליפא, who faced the challenge, cannot answer and stays quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a drill-hole equals a סלע, then בית שמאי (drill-hole) and בית הלל (סלע) would be saying the same size. But they are supposed to be arguing. The silence shows the challenge seems strong, which sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the hole in an animal's yoke
he was silent (he had no answer)

phrases.english: Like the full size of the hole of a yoke!
phrases.notes: The end of the challenge. This amud begins in the middle of the argument.

phrases.english: He was silent,
phrases.notes: רב תחליפא could not answer the challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a challenge that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית שמאי and בית הלל give different sizes (drill-hole versus סלע).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A drill-hole is the size of a yoke-hole, which equals a סלע. So the two measures are the same and the argument disappears.

steps.title: רב חסדא suggests the drill measure includes extra room
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא proposes that the measure is 'the drill and its חיסום.' This means the hole plus the extra space the drill needs, which is slightly bigger than a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said to him: Perhaps we learned 'a drill and its חיסום.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא steps in with a possible answer for the silent רב תחליפא. He suggests the measure is a hole wide enough for the drill to move in and out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole that only fits the drill tightly might equal a סלע. A hole with room for the drill to enter and come out is a bit larger. With that small difference, בית שמאי and בית הלל are giving different sizes again.

keyTerms.meaning: its 'closing' space: the extra room around the drill so it can go in and out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'מקדח וחיסומו' as two separate holes. It describes one hole that is slightly wider than the drill itself.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said to him:
Perhaps we learned 'a drill and its obstruction.'
phrases.notes: The hole includes room for the drill to be put in and taken out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that left רב תחליפא silent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The drill measure is just the drill's own hole, which equals a סלע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drill measure includes room for the drill to move in and out, so it is slightly larger than a סלע.

steps.title: רב תחליפא confirms the answer with certainty
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא says it is not 'perhaps' but definitely 'drill and its חיסום.' One can rely on this as surely as on the testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב תחליפא said to him: Do not say 'perhaps.' Rather, it is certainly 'a drill and its חיסום,' and one may rely on it like חזקיה אבי עקש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב תחליפא fully accepts רב חסדא's answer and upgrades it from a guess to a certainty. He compares its reliability to the well-known testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction is now settled: 'drill-hole' means a hole with room for the drill to go in and out. Following the same logic, the 'כרשינה' size in our משנה means a hole the vetch can go in and out of. Mentioning חזקיה אבי עקש sets up the next step, where the גמרא quotes his testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא whose testimony was accepted as reliable

steps.whatToRemember: A measure like 'the size of X' for a hole means a hole X can pass in and out of, not a tight fit. This applies to the drill and also to the כרשינה in our משנה.

phrases.english: And Rav Taḥlifa said to him:
Do not say 'perhaps,'
rather, it is certainly a drill and its obstruction,
one may rely on it
like the testimony of Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms and strengthens רב חסדא's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The drill measure of בית שמאי is 'drill and its חיסום,' slightly bigger than a סלע. Similarly, the כרשינה measure means a hole the vetch can go in and out of.

steps.title: The testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש about כלי חרס with no inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the testimony: a כלי חרס with no inside has no split between its sides. If one part becomes טמא, the whole thing becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: חזקיה אבי עקש gave this testimony before רבן גמליאל in יבנה, in the name of רבן גמליאל הזקן. Any כלי חרס that has no inside has no difference between its sides. If its inside becomes טמא, its outside becomes טמא. If its outside becomes טמא, its inside becomes טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reference to חזקיה אבי עקש by quoting his testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a כלי חרס with an inside follows a special rule: only its inside makes it טמא, and its outside is treated separately. This testimony says a flat כלי חרס with no inside is different. It has no 'front versus back' distinction, so טומאה on one side spreads to the whole vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned (in a תנאי source)

steps.confusionAlert: Read literally, the testimony seems to say a flat כלי חרס can become טמא. Step 5 challenges exactly that, and step 6 re-reads the testimony as being about a כלי שטף.

phrases.english: As we learned:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ עֵדוּת הֵעִיד חִזְקִיָּה אֲבִי עִקֵּשׁ
phrases.english: This testimony Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh testified
before Rabban Gamliel in Yavne,
which he said in the name of Rabban Gamliel the Elder:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס —
phrases.english: Any earthenware vessel that has no inside —
has no distinction for its outer sides.
phrases.notes: Inside and outside are not treated separately.

phrases.english: If its inside became impure, its outside became impure;
if its outside became impure, its inside became impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן זוֹ עֵדוּת הֵעִיד חִזְקִיָּה אֲבִי עִקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the testimony that רב תחליפא referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי חרס with no inside becomes completely טמא from either side. There is no split between inside and outside.

steps.title: Challenge: the Torah ties כלי חרס טומאה to its inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the testimony. The Torah makes a כלי חרס's טומאה depend on its inside, so one with no inside should not become טמא at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כלי חרס: the Torah made it depend on its inside. If it has an inside, it becomes טמא. If it has no inside, it should not become טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how a כלי חרס with no inside can become טמא at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'אל תוכו' (into its inside) shows that a כלי חרס gets טומאה only through its inside. So a vessel with no inside should not get טומאה at all, let alone become טמא on both sides. The answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: the Torah made it depend on
it has / it does not have

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge tests whether the testimony that רב תחליפא used as his standard of reliability really holds up.

phrases.english: An earthenware vessel: the Merciful One made it depend on its inside —
phrases.notes: Based on the פסוק 'אל תוכו' (ויקרא י״א:ל״ג).

phrases.english: if it has an inside, it becomes impure;

phrases.aramaic: לֵית לֵיהּ תּוֹךְ — לָא אִיטַּמִּי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: if it has no inside, it should not become impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the testimony quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a כלי חרס with no inside becomes טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah links a כלי חרס's טומאה to its inside. With no inside, there is nothing to make it טמא, so it should stay טהור.

steps.title: The testimony is really about a vessel that can be immersed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבין explains that the testimony is about a כלי שטף with no inside. Such a vessel can become טמא, and it has no split between its sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבין said: This is what the testimony means. Take any shape that would count as having no inside if it were a כלי חרס. A כלי שטף of that same shape has no split between its sides. If its inside becomes טמא, its back becomes טמא. If its back becomes טמא, its inside becomes טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבין answers the challenge from step 5 by changing which kind of vessel the testimony is about. It is about a כלי שטף, not a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי חרס with no inside cannot become טמא at all, so the challenge from step 5 was correct about that. But a כלי שטף, such as a wooden vessel, can become טמא even without an inside. For that kind of vessel, the testimony says the front and back are treated as one, so טומאה on either side spreads to the whole thing.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a re-reading of an earlier statement)
A vessel purified by immersion in a מקוה (wood, metal, and similar), as opposed to earthenware
The back or outer side of a vessel
Division; treating the sides as separate

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'בכלי חרס' are not the subject of the ruling. They only describe the shape: a shape that would count as having no inside if it were a כלי חרס. The ruling itself is about a כלי שטף.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avin said:
This is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס —
phrases.english: Any shape that has no inside in an earthenware vessel —
phrases.notes: This describes a shape that would never become טמא if it were earthenware.

phrases.english: its counterpart in an immersible vessel
phrases.notes: The real subject of the ruling.

phrases.english: has no division between its sides;
if its inside became impure, its back becomes impure;
if its back became impure, its inside becomes impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אָבִין: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by reading the testimony as being about a כלי שטף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the subject of the statement (changing the case it refers to)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The testimony is about a כלי חרס with no inside, which cannot become טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The testimony is about a כלי שטף with no inside, which can become טמא, and whose sides are not separated.

steps.title: Why mention earthenware at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the testimony refers to a כלי חרס if its ruling is about a כלי שטף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need to connect this to a כלי חרס? Let it simply say: any כלי שטף that has no inside has no split between its sides!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי יצחק בר אבין's reading. If the rule is about a כלי שטף, mentioning a כלי חרס seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The target is extra words in the testimony. A shorter wording that mentions only the כלי שטף would seem to say the same thing. Since every word should teach something, the reference to a כלי חרס needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks why something seems unnecessary)
To make it depend on; to connect it to

phrases.english: Why do I need to make it depend on an earthenware vessel?

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי שֶׁטֶף —
phrases.english: Let it say: any immersible vessel that has no inside —
has no division between its sides!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording implied by step 6's re-reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The mention of a כלי חרס in the testimony, as read by רבי יצחק בר אבין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ruling is about a כלי שטף, the mention of a כלי חרס adds nothing, so it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: An immersible vessel with an inside works like earthenware
steps.stepSummary: Mentioning a כלי חרס teaches that a כלי שטף that has an inside follows the כלי חרס rule. Its inside affects its outside, but its outside does not affect its inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us this: if a כלי שטף has an inside, it is like a כלי חרס. With a כלי חרס, if its inside became טמא, its back is טמא, and if its inside did not become טמא, its back is not טמא. So too with a כלי שטף: if its inside became טמא, its back is טמא, and if its inside did not become טמא, its back is not טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the כלי חרס is mentioned. It teaches a second rule about a כלי שטף that does have an inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two cases. A כלי שטף with no inside has no split: טומאה on either side makes the whole vessel טמא. A כלי שטף with an inside is compared to a כלי חרס: the inside is in charge, so טומאה inside reaches the back, but the inside stays טהור unless it was touched directly.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Just as... so too... (comparing two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי שטף with no inside: its sides are one, and either side makes the whole vessel טמא. A כלי שטף with an inside: like a כלי חרס, only טומאה on the inside spreads to the back.

phrases.english: This teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ תּוֹךְ — הֲרֵי הוּא כִּכְלִי חֶרֶס;
phrases.english: that if it has an inside, it is like an earthenware vessel;
just as with an earthenware vessel,
if its inside became impure, its back is impure,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — לֹא נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ;
phrases.english: if its inside did not become impure, its back is not impure;
so too an immersible vessel:
if its inside became impure, its back is impure,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — לֹא נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ.
phrases.english: if its inside did not become impure, its back is not impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by showing the mention of a כלי חרס teaches an additional rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording teaches a new rule (a comparison)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mention of a כלי חרס is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that a כלי שטף with an inside follows the כלי חרס pattern, where the inside controls the outside.

steps.title: The Torah said 'its inside' only about earthenware
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the comparison. The תורה limited טומאה to the inside only for a כלי חרס, not for a כלי שטף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a כלי חרס, because the רחמנא revealed 'its inside' about it. But for a כלי שטף, did the רחמנא reveal 'its inside' about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 8's comparison. It points out that the 'inside' rule comes from a verse that speaks only about a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a כלי חרס, the פסוק itself says the vessel becomes טמא through 'its inside.' No such verse exists for a כלי שטף. So טומאה touching a כלי שטף anywhere, even the outside, should make the whole vessel טמא, and the comparison to a כלי חרס seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for this case), but... (sets up a contrast)
The Merciful One, i.e., the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenges the source of the comparison in step 8. The גמרא will need to explain where a כלי שטף gets the 'inside' rule, or else change the reading.

phrases.english: It makes sense for an earthenware vessel,
since the Merciful One revealed 'its inside' regarding it,
but an immersible vessel,
did the Merciful One reveal 'its inside' regarding it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כְּלִי חֶרֶס, גַּלִּי בֵּיהּ רַחֲמָנָא תּוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a כלי שטף with an inside follows the כלי חרס rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'inside only' rule comes from a verse about a כלי חרס alone. With no such verse for a כלי שטף, there is no source for applying it there.

steps.title: The case is rabbinic טומאה from liquids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that with Torah-level טומאה a כלי שטף becomes טמא everywhere. But here the case is טומאת משקין, which is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we were talking about Torah-level impurity, you would be right. But here we are dealing with impurity from liquids, which is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 9. It does this by narrowing the case to a rabbinic kind of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was correct for Torah-level טומאה: there, a כלי שטף has no inside/outside split. The answer moves the case to טומאת משקין, which is only מדרבנן. That gives חז"ל room to set their own rules for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity passed on by impure liquids
"What case are we dealing with here?" (used to narrow the case)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not taking back what it said about כלי שטף. It agrees that under Torah law there is no split. It only says this case is a rabbinic one.

phrases.english: If it is referring to Torah-level impurity —
indeed, that is so (the whole vessel would be impure).
What case are we dealing with here?
With impurity from liquids, which is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּטוּמְאָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הָכִי נָמֵי, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): moves the case to rabbinic טומאה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling was about Torah-level טומאה, where the כלי חרס model does not fit a כלי שטף.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is about rabbinic טומאת משקין, where חז"ל could use the כלי חרס model.

steps.title: A משנה shows the inside/outside split for liquid טומאה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in כלים rules that when liquids make a vessel's outside טמא, only the outside is טמא. If the inside becomes טמא, the whole vessel is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: if the outside of a vessel became impure through liquids, its outside is impure. Its inside, rim, ear-handle, and straight handles stay pure. If its inside became impure, the whole thing is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up its answer. The משנה shows that liquid טומאה follows exactly the כלי חרס pattern, even for ordinary vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of any כלי, not only כלי חרס. Yet for liquid טומאה it gives the one-way rule: outside does not spread to inside, but inside spreads to everything. This is exactly the rule Step 8 claimed for a כלי שטף.

keyTerms.meaning: Its ear-shaped handle and its straight handles

phrases.english: As we learned: a vessel whose outside became impure through liquids —
its outside is impure;
its inside, its rim, its ear-handle, and its handles are pure.
If its inside became impure — all of it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 10
steps.raayaObject: That liquid טומאה on any vessel follows the one-way inside/outside rule

steps.title: By Torah law, food and liquid cannot make a vessel טמא
steps.stepSummary: By Torah law, food and liquids do not make vessels טמא. חז"ל made this גזירה because of the liquids of a זב and זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law, food does not make a vessel impure, and liquid does not make a vessel impure. It was the Rabbis who decreed this, because of the liquids of a זב and זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why liquid טומאה on a vessel is only rabbinic. This sets up the reason for the special rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary impure liquids are too weak to make a vessel טמא by Torah law. But the spit or urine of a זב or זבה is an אב הטומאה and does make vessels טמא. חז"ל made all impure liquids work this way so people would not confuse the two.

keyTerms.meaning: Food does not make a vessel impure
Liquids (spit, urine) of a זב or זבה, which are a primary source of impurity

phrases.english: By Torah law, food does not make a vessel impure,
and liquid does not make a vessel impure,
and it was the Rabbis who decreed it
because of the liquids of a זב and a זבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the background behind the משנה of Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liquid טומאה on vessels is only a rabbinic גזירה, made because of the liquids of a זב and זבה.

steps.title: So the Rabbis modeled it on כלי חרס
steps.stepSummary: Because this טומאה is rabbinic, חז"ל gave it the כלי חרס pattern. They did not give it the Torah-level rule of a כלי שטף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, the Rabbis treated it like the impurity of an earthenware vessel. They did not treat it like its own Torah-level impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion. Since חז"ל created this טומאה, they chose to follow the כלי חרס model for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Torah law, a טמא outside on a כלי שטף would make the whole vessel טמא. For this rabbinic טומאה, חז"ל chose the gentler כלי חרס pattern instead. That is how a כלי שטף can end up with an inside/outside split.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it (equal to), they treated it as

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי שטף that has an inside, touched on the outside by impure liquids, is only טמא on the outside, because חז"ל modeled this rabbinic טומאה on כלי חרס. (A כלי שטף with no inside becomes completely טמא, as the testimony says.)

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכָּךְ, שַׁוְּיוּהּ רַבָּנַן כְּטוּמְאָה דִּכְלִי חֶרֶס,
phrases.english: Therefore, the Rabbis made it like the impurity of an earthenware vessel,
and the Rabbis did not make it
like its own Torah-level impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ, שַׁוְּיוּהּ רַבָּנַן כְּטוּמְאָה דִּכְלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from Step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Rabbinic liquid טומאה on a כלי שטף follows the כלי חרס inside/outside rule.

steps.title: A sign so תרומה and קדשים are not burned
steps.stepSummary: חז"ל made a היכירא so people would know this טומאה is only rabbinic and would not burn תרומה or קדשים that touch the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis made a sign, so that people will not burn תרומה and קדשים because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason חז"ל chose the כלי חרס model. It acts as a visible sign that this is only rabbinic טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vessel were טמא all over, people might think it is Torah-level טמא. They would then burn תרומה or קדשים that touched it, even though by Torah law those items are טהור. The odd one-way rule reminds people that this טומאה is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn (impure תרומה and קדשים are burned)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: חז"ל sometimes shape a rabbinic law differently on purpose, so people will not treat it as Torah law and cause a real loss.

phrases.english: The Rabbis made a sign,
so that people will not burn
תרומה and consecrated items because of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling of Step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inside/outside split is a היכירא showing the טומאה is rabbinic, to protect תרומה and קדשים from being burned.

steps.title: Then a vessel with no inside should also get a sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if חז"ל made a היכירא here, they should make one for a vessel with no inside too. So why does the testimony say it becomes fully טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a vessel with no inside should also get a sign!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer using the original testimony. The testimony said a כלי שטף with no inside becomes טמא all over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the היכירא, protecting תרומה and קדשים, applies just as much to a vessel with no inside. So חז"ל should have kept part of that vessel טהור as a sign. But the testimony from Step 6 says the whole vessel is טמא, so the answer seems to clash with it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ נָמֵי,
phrases.english: If so, a vessel with no inside as well —
let them also make a sign!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ נָמֵי, לֶיעְבֵּיד נָמֵי הֶיכֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The היכירא explanation, set against the testimony about a כלי שטף with no inside (Step 6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same concern for תרומה and קדשים applies to a vessel with no inside. So a sign should be made there too, yet the testimony rules the whole vessel טמא.

steps.title: One sign is enough to show the whole rule is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: Since חז"ל made a היכירא for vessels that have an inside, everyone already knows that the טומאה of a vessel with no inside is also only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they made a sign for a vessel that has an inside, people will know that the vessel with no inside is also only טמא by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. It explains why vessels with no inside do not need their own sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign on vessels with an inside (only the outside becomes טמא) teaches people that liquids make vessels טמא only מדרבנן. Once people learn this, they will treat every case of this טומאה as rabbinic, including vessels with no inside. So no one will come to burn תרומה or קדשים because of it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign or marker that shows people something
A vessel that has an inside (a container)
A vessel with no inside (a flat item)

phrases.english: Since they made a sign
for a vessel that has an inside,
phrases.notes: Only the outside becomes טמא, which works as the sign

phrases.english: it is known that a vessel with no inside is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: One sign in one case teaches about the whole category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each kind of vessel would need its own sign
steps.terutzMaskana: The sign on vessels with an inside already shows that the whole rule is rabbinic

steps.title: Can a flat כלי שטף become טמא at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a כלי שטף with no inside can be טמא even from the Torah, since the Torah requires a vessel to be like a שק, which is carried both full and empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כלי שטף with no inside, can it become טמא from the Torah? We need it to be like a sack. Just as a sack is carried full and empty, so too anything must be carried full and empty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the case itself. A flat vessel cannot be carried full, so how can it become טמא at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists שק among things that become טמא. From this we learn that a vessel must be able to be moved both when full and when empty. A flat item with no inside cannot hold anything, so it seems it cannot become טמא even מדאורייתא. If so, why would חז"ל need to make a rule about its outside?

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel purified by rinsing in a מקוה (wood, metal, cloth, leather)
Carried around both full and empty

phrases.english: And a rinsable vessel with no inside,
is it able to receive impurity by Torah law?
We require it to be similar to a sack,
just as a sack is carried full and empty,
so too anything must be carried full and empty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי שֶׁטֶף, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בַּר קַבּוֹלֵי טוּמְאָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case behind the answer in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a כלי שטף with no inside can become טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שק rule says only things carried full and empty become טמא, and a flat item cannot be carried full

steps.title: The case is a flat vessel fit for sitting
steps.stepSummary: The case is a flat vessel used for sitting or lying, which can become טמא through מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking of those that are fit for מדרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is a flat item made for sitting or lying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item made for sitting or lying becomes טמא through מדרס of a זב or זבה, even without an inside. So it can be טמא from the Torah, and the rabbinic rule about liquids can apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: טומאה from a זב or זבה sitting, lying, or leaning on an item

phrases.english: With those that are fit for treading-impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any flat כלי שטף is meant, and it cannot be טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is flat items fit for מדרס, which can be טמא from the Torah

steps.title: Then flat כלי חרס should be the same
steps.stepSummary: If a flat item fit for sitting can be טמא, a flat כלי חרס fit for sitting should also get the rabbinic liquid טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, earthenware too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If being fit for sitting is the reason, it should apply to clay items too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 18 depends on מדרס. A flat clay item can also be sat on. So why was only the כלי שטף included in the rabbinic rule for vessels with no inside?

phrases.english: If so, earthenware too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A flat clay item can also be sat on, so the same rule should apply to it

steps.title: Clay vessels never get מדרס
steps.stepSummary: כלי חרס never becomes טמא through מדרס, so a flat clay item has no way to be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no מדרס for earthenware vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Clay items do not become טמא through מדרס at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי חרס becomes טמא only through its inside. Sitting on it does not make it טמא. So a flat clay item cannot become טמא in any way, and חז"ל had no reason to include it in the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A clay vessel, which becomes טמא only from its inside

steps.whatToRemember: A flat כלי שטף fit for מדרס can be טמא, so חז"ל included it in the liquid rule. A flat כלי חרס can never be טמא, so it is left out.

phrases.english: There is no treading-impurity in earthenware vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Clay items fit for sitting should be like a כלי שטף
steps.terutzMaskana: מדרס does not apply to כלי חרס, so the comparison fails

steps.title: רב פפא: the teaching was about a large drill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier skull discussion. רב פפא says the teaching that set the drill-hole equal to a סלע was speaking about a large drill.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We learned about a large drill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the vessels topic and goes back to the earlier question about a skull with a missing piece. It now gives another answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי give the missing amount as the size of a drill-hole. According to שמואל, בית הלל give it as a סלע. Another teaching said a drill-hole and a סלע are the same size, which would mean there is no argument. רב פפא answers that the teaching was about a large drill. בית שמאי meant a smaller drill, so the two opinions really are different.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin, used here as a measure of size
An אמורא who gives this answer

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not about vessels. It goes back to an earlier topic, the skull with a missing piece.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We learned about a large drill.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַקְדֵּחַ גָּדוֹל שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the vessels discussion and goes back to the earlier skull question with a new answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the source as speaking about a specific size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The drill-hole and the סלע are always the same size, so בית שמאי and בית הלל would agree
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching about the סלע meant a large drill, while בית שמאי meant a smaller one, so the dispute is real

steps.title: So an ordinary drill is smaller than a סלע
steps.stepSummary: From רב פפא's answer, the גמרא infers that an unspecified drill-hole is smaller than a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: This shows that a plain, unspecified drill is also smaller than a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רב פפא's answer. If only a large drill equals a סלע, then a regular drill must be smaller than a סלע. This inference sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said the source equating drill and סלע meant a large drill. So when בית שמאי say just 'a drill' with no size given, they mean something smaller than בית הלל's סלע. This is how the two opinions become truly different.

keyTerms.meaning: A drill, here meaning the size of the hole it makes
Plain or unspecified, with no size stated
A coin, used here as a measure of size

phrases.english: By inference, that an unspecified drill
is also smaller than a sela.
phrases.notes: So בית שמאי's 'drill' is a smaller measure than בית הלל's סלע.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּמַקְדֵּחַ סְתָם זוּטַרא נָמֵי מִכְּסֶלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what follows from רב פפא's answer in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified drill-hole is smaller than a סלע.

steps.title: This fits רבי מאיר, but what about the Sages?
steps.stepSummary: The inference works for רבי מאיר, who says בית שמאי meant a small doctors' drill. According to the חכמים, בית שמאי meant the large drill of the לשכה, which equals a סלע, so the dispute disappears.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי מאיר. But what can be said according to the חכמים? As the משנה teaches: Which drill did they mean? The small drill of doctors. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: the large drill of the לשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about which drill בית שמאי meant. It then shows that the חכמים's view brings back the original problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, בית שמאי meant a small drill, so their measure is smaller than a סלע and the two sides really disagree. For the חכמים, בית שמאי meant the large drill. A large drill equals a סלע, so בית שמאי and בית הלל would be saying the same size.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (a challenge)
A chamber in the Temple, whose drill was large

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Meir,
but according to the Rabbis, what is there to say?
As we learned: Regarding which drill did they speak?
phrases.notes: The source is משנה אהלות ב:ג.

phrases.english: Regarding the small one used by doctors,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: regarding the large one of the chamber.
phrases.notes: A large drill equals a סלע, so there would be no real dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the inference in step 22 fails according to the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's answer, as explained by the inference in step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים say בית שמאי meant the large drill. A large drill equals a סלע, so בית שמאי and בית הלל would give the same measure.

steps.title: Even for רבי מאיר it causes a problem
steps.stepSummary: If בית שמאי's drill is smaller than בית הלל's סלע, then בית שמאי would be the lenient side. That case is not on the closed list of places where בית שמאי are lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does it really work for רבי מאיר? It would become one of the leniencies of בית שמאי and stringencies of בית הלל. And we have a rule: what was taught on that list was taught, and what was not taught was not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges רבי מאיר too. His reading would make בית שמאי more lenient than בית הלל here, which goes against an accepted rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A skull missing a piece of this size does not make a tent טמא. The smaller the missing piece needed, the more lenient the opinion. For רבי מאיר, בית שמאי need only a small hole, so they are lenient. But the list of בית שמאי's leniencies in מסכת עדיות is closed, and this case is not on it.

keyTerms.term: מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
keyTerms.meaning: Among the cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict

keyTerms.term: דִּתְנַן תְּנַן, דְּלָא תְּנַן לָא תְּנַן
keyTerms.meaning: Only what is on the list counts; nothing can be added to it

steps.confusionAlert: The missing size is what makes the skull lose its טומאה. So a SMALLER required size is the LENIENT opinion, not the strict one.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir, does it work out well?
It would be among the leniencies of Beit Shammai
and the stringencies of Beit Hillel.
And we hold: what we learned, we learned,
phrases.notes: This refers to the list in מסכת עדיות.

phrases.english: and what we did not learn, we did not learn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the challenge from the חכמים to רבי מאיר as well.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reading that בית שמאי's drill is smaller than a סלע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A smaller measure makes בית שמאי lenient. But the list of בית שמאי's leniencies is closed, and this case is not on it.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the equal סלע was a Neronian סלע
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the סלע that equals a large drill is a large Neronian סלע. An ordinary סלע is smaller than even an ordinary drill, so בית שמאי stay the stricter side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The סלע we learned is like a large drill is a Neronian סלע. An ordinary סלע is smaller than an ordinary drill.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the challenges by saying that two different coins are involved. Only the big Neronian סלע matches the large drill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's measure is an ordinary סלע, and it is smaller than any drill. So בית הלל need a smaller missing piece, which makes them the lenient side, and בית שמאי are strict. This answers the problem for רבי מאיר and keeps the closed list intact. It also creates a real dispute even for the חכמים, since their large drill is still bigger than an ordinary סלע.

keyTerms.meaning: A large סלע coin minted by the emperor Nero

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן: ordinary סלע < any drill ≤ large drill = Neronian סלע. So בית שמאי (drill) are stricter than בית הלל (ordinary סלע).
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps בית שמאי as the stricter side and so protects the rule that the list of בית שמאי's leniencies is closed.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
It is a Neronian sela that we learned
as being like a large drill;
an ordinary sela is smaller than an ordinary drill.
phrases.notes: So בית הלל's measure is the smaller one, and בית שמאי are strict.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: סֶלַע נִירוֹנִית שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges in steps 23 and 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the source refers to a special kind of coin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the סלע equal to a large drill was the same ordinary סלע that בית הלל used.
steps.terutzMaskana: The equal סלע is the large Neronian one. An ordinary סלע is smaller than any drill, so בית שמאי are stricter for both רבי מאיר and the חכמים.

steps.title: Damage to the eyelid is a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with eyelid damage: an eyelid that was pierced, damaged, or split counts as a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An eyelid that was pierced, that was damaged, or that was split.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here and moves on to eye blemishes. Its first cases are about the eyelid: a hole, a missing piece, or a split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are three kinds of physical damage to the eyelid itself. Each one is enough to make the animal blemished, so a בכור with it may be slaughtered outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The earlier skull and drill-hole discussion is finished. This is a brand-new משנה about the eye, not a continuation of that argument.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The eyelid that was pierced,
that was damaged, that was split,
phrases.notes: The same eyelid with a piece missing, or with a crack

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The skull and drill-hole sugya is complete.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An eyelid that is pierced, damaged, or split is a מום.

steps.title: Growths and marks inside the eye
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more eye blemishes: a דק, a תבלול, and growths shaped like a snail, a snake, or a berry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, if there is in his eye a cataract, a תבלול, a snail, a snake, or a berry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing eye blemishes. This time they are things that appear inside the eye itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 was about damage to the eyelid. These cases are about marks or growths on the eye itself, which often cover the pupil. The snail, snake, and berry are named after the shape of the growth.

keyTerms.meaning: A cataract or film over the eye
A white thread-like line in the eye (defined in the next steps)
A growth shaped like a snail
A growth shaped like a snake
A growth shaped like a berry

phrases.english: if there is in his eye a cataract, a tevallul,
a snail, a snake, a berry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list. It moves from the eyelid to the eye itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A דק, a תבלול, or a snail-, snake-, or berry-shaped growth in the eye is a מום.

steps.title: What exactly is a תבלול?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה stops to ask what a תבלול is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a תבלול?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה itself asks a short question to define an unclear word from its list. It is setting up the definition that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of all the items in the list, the תבלול is the one that needs a precise description. The exact look of the mark decides whether it counts as a מום, so the definition matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one is it? / What is it?

phrases.english: What is a tevallul?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of one term from the list in step 27.

steps.title: A white line crossing into the black
steps.stepSummary: A תבלול is a white line that cuts through the iris and enters the black pupil.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a white line that cuts across the iris and enters the black.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question and defines the תבלול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details are required. The line must be white, and it must run from the iris into the black part of the eye.

keyTerms.meaning: The iris (the colored ring around the pupil)
The black part of the eye (the pupil)

phrases.english: A white line that cuts across the iris
and enters the black.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A white line that cuts through the iris and enters the black pupil.

steps.title: A black line entering the white is not a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The reverse case, a black line running into the white of the eye, is not a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a black line enters the white, it is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets a limit on the definition. The opposite pattern does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The direction and color of the line are what matter. A white mark that reaches into the black pupil is a מום. A black mark that reaches into the white is not.
steps.whatToRemember: Eye blemishes include damage to the eyelid and growths in the eye. A תבלול is specifically a white line going into the black. A black line going into the white is not a מום.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume any line crossing between black and white is a תבלול. Only a white line entering the black counts.

phrases.english: If a black line enters the white —
it is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of the definition given in step 29 by ruling out the reverse case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A black line entering the white of the eye is not a מום.
